title: Integration: run the Dummit & Foote / James Bond test case end-to-end through producer and blind checker
description:
The epic's explicit TEST CASE (bd show teach-8xw): "Teach Dummit & Foote to a
learner whose stated interest is James Bond. The checker must confirm the
algebra is correct and the prerequisites were really established -- not
that the Bond framing was enjoyable." This is the acceptance test for the
whole system and nothing exists yet to run it against.

This is necessarily last in the dependency chain: it needs a real graph
(teach-8xw.5) covering at least the relevant D&F prerequisite chain (note:
undergraduate abstract algebra is beyond the VA K-12 SOL the graph is
seeded from, so this may also require extending the graph beyond SOL scope
-- flag that gap explicitly if/when hit, don't silently reinterpret the test
case to fit only K-12 content), a working persona/narrative renderer
(teach-8xw.6) with CBT primitives (teach-8xw.7) and the bounded Cialdini
layer (teach-8xw.8), and a working blind checker (teach-8xw.9, .10, .11,
.13) on the other side.

What would close this: an actual run producing lesson text for a real D&F
concept in Bond framing, fed to the checker with zero access to producer
state, where the checker's report is captured and honestly reflects
whatever it did or didn't confirm -- per sandbox-prompt.md, this must be
reported as "this is what was covered, this is what wasn't," never phrased
as a blanket pass.

title: Checker: define the blind interface boundary (lesson text only, no producer state)
description:
CLAUDE.md and sandbox-prompt.md both state the core architectural
requirement of this whole repo: "the checker does not get access to the
producer's internals... A checker that can read the producer's state will
agree with it and verify nothing." Nothing has been built yet, so this
boundary does not exist in any form -- there is no producer output format,
no checker input format, no enforcement that they stay separated.

This should be filed and resolved before either producer or checker code
starts accumulating, because it is much cheaper to fix an interface before
two halves of a codebase grow around it than after.

What would close this: a fixed artifact format for "what the learner saw"
(e.g. plain lesson text, or a transcript structure with only
learner-visible fields), with a runnable check that fails if any field
reachable from that artifact (by static inspection, e.g. grepping the
producer's output schema/dataclass) contains planner-only fields like
target node id, traversal, or answer key. This check is what makes the
producer/checker split enforced rather than just a convention someone can
accidentally break later.
close_reason: Blind interface boundary defined and enforced: teach/boundary.py (LessonArtifact type + check_no_forbidden_fields static detector), teach/producer_state.py (realistic leaky PlannerState fixture + emit_lesson_artifact crossing point), tests/test_boundary.py (7 passing tests including proof the detector fires on real and nested leaks, not just vacuous passes). See sandbox-handoffs/teach-8xw.9.md.

title: Producer: define a checkable honesty constraint before building the Cialdini motivation layer
description:
The epic (bd show teach-8xw) requires motivation to be "guided by Cialdini's
Influence and Pre-Suasion... bounded by a hard honesty constraint," and
sandbox-prompt.md is explicit this is "a checkable property, not a tone
note." Nothing exists yet. This is the highest-risk component in the whole
system: a persuasion layer is exactly the machinery capable of making an
overstated claim about a learner's potential feel true, which is the one
thing the checker (teach-8xw.12) must be able to catch from text alone.

Filing this as a design bead ahead of implementation because building the
persuasion techniques (reciprocity, commitment/consistency, social proof,
liking, authority, scarcity, unity) without first fixing a concrete,
checkable definition of "honest claim about potential" risks producing
output that is fluent and persuasive but structurally impossible for the
blind checker to evaluate consistently.

What would close this: a concrete rubric (recorded via `bd update --design`
on this bead) for what makes a statement about learner potential "honest" --
e.g. it must be conditioned on effort ("if you practice X you can reach Y"),
must not claim a ceiling higher than what's evidenced by the learner's
actual measured performance in-session, etc. -- specific enough that
teach-8xw.12 (the overpromise detector) can be implemented directly against
it, not against a vague restatement of "don't lie."
design:
Honesty rubric for statements about learner potential, implemented in
teach/honesty_rubric.py (decision function `classify`, worked examples in
`WORKED_EXAMPLES`, tests in tests/test_honesty_rubric.py -- 16 passing).

CLAIM SHAPE. A PotentialClaim is any lesson-text statement asserting what
the learner can/will/is capable of. Four kinds a checker must distinguish
when extracting from text: GROWTH (developable capability), OUTCOME
(specific future result/reward), TRAIT (innate fixed characteristic offered
as the reason for an outcome), COMPARATIVE (likened to a named exceptional
person/standard).

THREE ATTRIBUTES, ALL ANSWERABLE FROM TEXT ALONE (the checker has nothing
else per teach-8xw.9's boundary):
  - conditioned_on_effort: bool -- does the claim explicitly tie the outcome
    to described effort/practice, vs asserting it as inevitable/innate?
  - evidenced_ceiling: bool | None -- is the claimed ceiling no higher than
    what's already evidenced by demonstrated performance present in the
    SAME lesson text, or an ordinary extension of it? None when the text
    gives no basis to decide (abstention case).
  - claim_type: one of the four kinds above.

DECISION TABLE (classify()):
  1. claim_type is TRAIT -> always INFLATED. Hard rule, independent of the
     other two attributes -- a fixed-trait framing bypasses effort by
     construction, so no ceiling modesty rescues it.
  2. not conditioned_on_effort -> INFLATED. An unconditioned promise about
     the future is a guarantee, checked before evidenced_ceiling even
     matters.
  3. Otherwise: evidenced_ceiling is None -> ABSTAIN. evidenced_ceiling is
     False -> INFLATED. evidenced_ceiling is True -> HONEST.

WORKED EXAMPLES (6, in teach/honesty_rubric.py, reusable by teach-8xw.13
per its own acceptance criteria):
  - HONEST: growth claim conditioned on effort, next step is an ordinary
    extension of something the learner just did in the same transcript.
  - INFLATED (unconditioned outcome): "best mathematician of your
    generation" with no effort framing.
  - INFLATED (trait): "born to understand abstract algebra."
  - INFLATED (conditioned but unevidenced ceiling): "publishing original
    research... by next month" off one lesson's exercises.
  - INFLATED (unconditioned comparative): "basically the next Emmy
    Noether."
  - ABSTAIN: "You'll get there" -- conditioned, but too vague to check
    against anything evidenced.

NOTE FOR teach-8xw.13: this bead defines the decision procedure over
already-extracted attributes; it deliberately does NOT parse raw lesson
text to populate claim_type/conditioned_on_effort/evidenced_ceiling -- that
extraction, including the judgment call that COMPARATIVE claims will almost
never satisfy evidenced_ceiling=True in a real transcript (matching a named
historical figure's actual achievement is a categorically higher bar than
one lesson can evidence), is .13's scope.
close_reason: Rubric defined in teach/honesty_rubric.py (classify() decision table + 6 worked examples), 9 passing tests in tests/test_honesty_rubric.py, full rubric text recorded via bd update --design. teach-8xw.13 now unblocked.

title: Locate the 'narrator' story-generation package the persona layer must reuse
description:
Problem: the epic (bd show teach-8xw) requires the producer's persona layer to
render graph traversals as narrative by "reusing the story-generation
machinery from narrator (motive graph, personality as data structure) rather
than reimplementing it." No such package exists anywhere in this sandbox.

How I confirmed this:
- `find / -maxdepth 3 -iname "*narrator*"` (excluding /proc) returned nothing.
- `bd memories narrator` returned no results.
- GitHub code/repo search `narrator story generation motive graph` via
  `curl https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=...` returned
  total_count: 0.
- PyPI has a package literally named `narrator` (200 on
  https://pypi.org/pypi/narrator/json) but nothing in its name suggests it is
  a "motive graph / personality as data structure" story engine; almost
  certainly unrelated and should not be assumed to be the intended dependency
  without checking its actual contents.

This blocks any real implementation of the persona/narrative-rendering stage
(see the "Producer: persona / narrative rendering layer" bead) -- there is
nothing to import and no spec to reimplement against.

What would close this:
- Either a confirmed location for the actual `narrator` project (a repo URL,
  a package registry entry verified to match the motive-graph/personality
  description, or explicit human direction to vendor/reimplement a minimal
  subset), OR
- An explicit human decision (via `bd human`) that narrator is unavailable
  and the persona layer should be built standalone, with a note on what
  subset of "motive graph as data structure" it must satisfy.

Do not start building the persona layer until one of the above is resolved --
building against a guessed API would produce integration work that has to be
redone.
notes:
CONFIRMED (2026-09-08): mount is real, human's file pointers verified by reading
+ executing narrator's own self-checks (uv run --with networkx python3 motive.py
-> "ok"; ocean.py, evidence_ledger.py, admissibility.py -> "ok").

Ground truth correction: narrator/prd.md says what narrator actually is -- a
teaching project for three teenagers to learn code-generation-meets-psychology
by building a murder-mystery motive simulator. It is NOT a generic, importable
"render any graph traversal as narrative" library with a clean public API. The
epic's phrase "reusing narrator's story-generation machinery" cannot mean
"import narrator and call a function" -- there is no such function. It means:
take the specific reusable pieces, vendor or reimplement them; treat the rest
as pattern to imitate, not code to call.

REUSABLE AS-IS (vendor into teach, no rewrite needed):
- ocean.py -- OCEAN 5-vector -> system_prompt()/options(), zero mystery-domain
  coupling, stdlib+dataclasses only. This literally IS "personality as data
  structure." CultureMatrix's mandatory-citation gate is a policy teach should
  keep (no uncited persona-adaptation coefficients).
- backends/base.py (Backend protocol) + backends/ocean_ollama.py -- the
  profile-in/text-out seam. Directly usable for calling a model to render
  persona-flavored lesson text.

PATTERN TO IMITATE, NOT CODE TO IMPORT:
- motive.py's traversal engine (load_graph/deterioration_path/to_mermaid):
  weighted-random walk from an entry-kind node to a terminal-kind node,
  no-revisit, seeded-reproducible, JSON-schema-validated-on-load, Mermaid
  render with the walked path highlighted. motive_graph.json's *content* is
  murder-motive vocabulary -- entirely inapplicable to lesson content. Teach
  needs its own traversal-to-narrative-beats function built the same way,
  running over mathgraph's prerequisite DAG (already a different edge
  semantics: depends_on/authored vs aligns_to/inferred, see mathgraph/graph.py
  -- not an escalation-weighted walk, closer to a topo-respecting path).
- admissibility.py + evidence_ledger.py: the producer/checker grounding
  pattern (provenance-tagged claims; DIRECT vs DERIVED; recursive grounding
  check blind to the model's internal reasoning) is the closest existing
  analog to what teach's blind checker must do for lesson claims vs assumed
  prerequisites. Needs a from-scratch teach-domain version (ledger of lesson
  claims, not clue evidence) -- code itself is not reusable, the shape is.
- mathgraph/align.py's three-valued MATCHED/AMBIGUOUS/UNMATCHED abstention
  (thresholds tau_cov/delta_margin fitted to a target precision, not hand-
  picked) is the abstention shape teach-8xw.10/.11 should copy for e.g.
  "which prerequisite node does this lesson text actually establish."

NOT REUSABLE AT ALL: mystery.py, clue_partition.py, hypothesis_board.py,
question_selector.py, panel.py, chapters.py, turn.py, discussion.py, agents.py,
moves.py, metrics.py -- all are murder-mystery-gameplay-specific (suspects,
clues, interrogation turns). Not inspected in depth; named here only so a
future session doesn't re-open this question for them without cause.

This closes teach-8xw.1: confirmed location + confirmed reusable/build-new
split, satisfying the bead's own closing criterion. teach-8xw.6 unblocks.
close_reason: Confirmed: narrator is real, local, mounted read-only at /workspace-narrator. Read + executed its self-checks (all pass). Determined and documented the reusable-as-is vs pattern-to-imitate vs must-build-new split (ocean.py + backends/ reusable as-is; motive.py traversal, admissibility/evidence_ledger grounding, mathgraph align.py abstention are patterns to imitate not code to call). Full breakdown on the bead notes and sandbox-handoffs/teach-8xw.1.md.

title: Survey existing VA Math SOL prerequisite knowledge graphs before building one
description:
Problem: the epic says to plan instruction as traversal of a mathgraph-style
prerequisite DAG "seeded from the Virginia Mathematics Standards of Learning"
and explicitly says: "Look for an existing graph that already covers the VA
SOL before building one." No such search had been done yet.

What I did this session (shallow first pass, not exhaustive):
- Queried the HuggingFace datasets API directly (WebSearch tool in this
  sandbox is non-functional -- it returns a canned "I can't search" refusal
  on every query; use `curl` against `https://huggingface.co/api/datasets?search=...`
  instead, which does work, network egress confirmed via
  `curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://huggingface.co` -> 200):
  - `search=mathgraph` -> alinasdkey/mathGraphs (0 downloads-ish, no
    description, unclear content), uw-math-ai/math-graph and
    jessteru/math-graph (both "TheoremGraph": a statement-level dependency
    graph over arXiv math papers and Lean 4 formalizations -- research/
    undergrad-and-up formal math, NOT K-12 SOL-seeded, no evident tie to VA
    SOL codes).
  - `search=prerequisite graph math` -> zero results.
  - `search=virginia sol` -> zero results.
- Conclusion from this pass: nothing found on HuggingFace that is seeded from
  or mapped to the VA Math SOL. This is NOT a thorough survey -- it only hit
  the HF dataset search API with three query strings.

What would close this:
- A wider survey (GitHub repos, Papers with Code, VDOE/Virginia Department of
  Education published resources, other states' math standards graphs that
  might be adaptable, general "knowledge graph for K-12 math" literature)
  that either finds a reusable graph (record its location, license, and
  coverage gaps against the VA SOL) or documents the negative result across
  all channels checked, clearing the way to build one from scratch.
- Note in whichever direction: the "publish to HuggingFace" epic goal and
  the "find or stand up a common reference site for existing knowledge
  graphs in an AI-consumable format" epic goal are separate from this --
  filed separately, see the "common reference site" bead.
notes:
SURVEY COMPLETE. Full write-up: sandbox-handoffs/teach-8xw.2.md

Bottom line: no existing graph is seeded from / directly usable as a VA Math
SOL prerequisite DAG. But found a near-miss that changes what "build from
scratch" should mean for teach-8xw.5:

1. github.com/learning-commons-org/knowledge-graph (CC BY-4.0, active,
   v1.13.0/2026-08-27) has real VA Math SOL standard text: 1,759 nodes,
   correct statementCodes (e.g. 2.NS.3f), attributed to VDOE source docs.
   Verified by downloading both full JSONL exports (343MB+571MB) and
   indexing every edge touching those 1,759 node ids: 0 prerequisite edges
   (buildsTowards), 0 crosswalk edges to Common Core (hasStandardAlignment
   -- VA is one of the states absent from that table entirely, consistent
   with VA never adopting Common Core), 0 of any other relation type except
   hasChild (outline hierarchy, not prerequisites). The nodes exist; the
   edges teach-8xw.5 needs don't.

2. The 757 buildsTowards edges that DO exist in that same dataset are all
   Common-Core-only, and are the same Student-Achievement-Partners
   "Coherence Map" dataset independently vendored (CC0) at
   github.com/markpaik/coherence-map-explorer (480 CCSS standards, 757
   edges, DAG-verified). Reusable prerequisite structure exists for K-12
   math -- just not for SOL, and no VA-SOL-to-CCSS crosswalk was found
   anywhere searched (VDOE site 403s bots; Wayback CDX search of
   doe.virginia.gov for crosswalk/comparison/commoncore/vertical/progression
   terms: zero hits on all five).

3. Widened search beyond the prior session's 3 HF queries to 11 more HF
   queries, 7 GitHub repo-search queries, arXiv, and VDOE-via-Wayback.
   Only other real hit: haojing8312/cn-k12-math-knowledge-graph, a
   well-built Chinese K1-9 prerequisite graph -- wrong curriculum/language,
   not reusable content, but a nice structural precedent (leaves
   zero-in-degree topics "unresolved" rather than asserting no-prerequisite).

4. teach-8xw.3 (common reference site bead) should look hard at Learning
   Commons -- it explicitly positions itself as exactly that (multi-state,
   multi-subject, graph-native, public JSONL). Not acted on here, flagged
   for whoever picks up .3.

5. Tooling note: WebSearch is non-functional in this sandbox (canned
   non-answers, one fabricated-looking URL presented as a real search hit
   -- confirmed fake via Wayback: zero snapshots ever). Matches prior
   session's WebFetch-hallucination finding on teach-8xw.1. Use curl against
   real APIs (HF datasets API, GitHub API, Wayback CDX/availability API,
   arXiv export API) instead.

No code touched. uv run pytest -q: 16 passed, unchanged.
close_reason: Survey complete per acceptance criteria: found the closest existing candidate (Learning Commons KG has real VA SOL Math content but zero prerequisite/crosswalk edges), documented its location/license/coverage gap, and documented the negative result (no ready-made VA SOL prerequisite DAG) across HuggingFace, GitHub, arXiv, and VDOE-via-Wayback. Clears the way for teach-8xw.5 to build from scratch, informed by what's actually missing (edges, not standard text).

title: Checker: flag promises about learner potential that outrun what effort can deliver
description:
Checker stage, per the epic (bd show teach-8xw): "flag any promise about the
learner's potential that outruns what effort can deliver." Nothing exists
yet. This is the checker-side counterpart to teach-8xw.8 (the producer-side
honesty rubric) -- it must be implemented directly against whatever concrete
rubric that bead settles on, not against an independent guess at "sounds
like an overpromise," or the two halves will disagree on the boundary.
Blocked on teach-8xw.8 for that reason.

What would close this: given lesson text, flags statements about learner
potential that violate the teach-8xw.8 rubric, with a runnable check using a
hand-written honest-encouragement example (should pass clean) and a
hand-written inflated-promise example (should be flagged).
design: Implemented in teach/potential_checker.py: extract_claims() heuristically extracts PotentialClaim from raw lesson text (tutor-only turns, sentence-level pattern matching for TRAIT/COMPARATIVE/GROWTH/OUTCOME, effort-conditioning phrase list, evidenced_ceiling from a categorical-too-high pattern list + comparative-always-false + just-did/next ordinary-extension pattern, else None). check_lesson_text() runs classify() on each and surfaces non-HONEST verdicts as Flag. Validated end-to-end against 5/6 of teach-8xw.8's WORKED_EXAMPLES (exact verdict match) plus 2 new hand-written examples (honest transcript passes clean, inflated transcript flagged). The 6th worked example ('You'll get there.') is deliberately excluded as text-ambiguous on conditioned_on_effort (a plain bool with no abstain state) -- extractor abstains a different way, by not extracting vague filler as a claim at all. 16 new tests in tests/test_potential_checker.py, 32 total passing.
notes: Closing: acceptance criteria met (extraction + classify against teach-8xw.8 rubric, hand-written honest example passes clean, hand-written inflated example flagged, runnable self-check + pytest suite). Full detail in sandbox-handoffs/teach-8xw.13.md.
close_reason: Acceptance criteria met: extractor + classifier implemented against the teach-8xw.8 rubric, validated against 5/6 canonical worked examples plus new hand-written honest/inflated examples, 32 tests passing.

title: Publishing: HuggingFace publish pipeline for built knowledge graphs
description:
Epic PUBLISHING goal (bd show teach-8xw): "Publish graphs we build to
HuggingFace (HF_TOKEN is forwarded)." Confirmed the forwarding is already
wired at the infra level: pyproject.toml has
`[tool.sandbox.forward-env]` / `HF_TOKEN = "why this matters when unset"`,
but there is no code anywhere in the repo that uses it -- no huggingface_hub
dependency in pyproject.toml (dependencies = [] currently), no publish
script.

Blocked on teach-8xw.5 (there has to be a built graph to publish) and
implicitly informed by teach-8xw.3 (the "common reference site" survey may
determine the target schema/format other consumers expect).

What would close this: a script that takes the graph artifact and pushes it
as a HuggingFace dataset, with a dry-run mode that doesn't require a live
HF_TOKEN (so it's testable without live credentials), and a runnable check
covering at least the dry-run path.
notes: Done. teach/publish_graph.py: build_dataset_files() (pure/offline/deterministic) + publish() (dry_run defaults True whenever no HF_TOKEN, dry-run path touches no network). CLI: python3 -m teach.publish_graph --repo-id ... [--live]. Added huggingface-hub dep via uv add. 11 new tests in tests/test_publish_graph.py, all run with HF_TOKEN unset. env -u HF_TOKEN uv run pytest -q: 90 passed (79 pre-existing + 11 new). Filed teach-8xw.17 for live-push verification (needs a real HF_TOKEN this session didn't have) -- not required for this bead's acceptance criteria. Handoff: sandbox-handoffs/teach-8xw.14.md

title: Checker: recover taught concept and assumed prerequisites from lesson text alone
description:
Checker stage, per the epic (bd show teach-8xw): given only emitted lesson
text (via the boundary defined in teach-8xw.9), independently recover which
concept was taught and which prerequisites were assumed -- without seeing
the planner's target node or traversal. Nothing exists yet.

This is a genuinely hard inference task, not a lookup: it has to work from
prose/narrative framing (per the epic's Bond-framed Dummit & Foote test
case) and identify the underlying concept graph position without being
handed it. Depends on teach-8xw.9 (needs the fixed blind-input format to
build against) and, for evaluation, on teach-8xw.5 (needs real graph nodes
to check recovered concepts against).

What would close this: given a small fixed set of hand-written lesson texts
with known ground truth (concept + prerequisite set), the recovery step
identifies them correctly, or explicitly abstains ("cannot tell") rather
than guessing wrong -- per sandbox-prompt.md's "prefer abstention to a
confident answer." A runnable check exercising at least the abstention path
and one correct-recovery path.
close_reason: Built teach/concept_recovery.py (domain-agnostic vocabulary-overlap recovery engine with document-frequency boilerplate filtering, dual abstention gates for taught-concept match, phrase+vocabulary gated assumed-prerequisite recovery restricted to direct edges) + tests/test_concept_recovery.py (10 tests) exercising the bead's required correct-recovery path (VA Math SOL 4.MG recovered with 3.MG as assumed prerequisite) and abstention path (group-theory/Bond-flavored text abstains against the K-8 math graph, reproducing the documented D&F-out-of-scope gap teach-8xw.15 names). uv run pytest -q: 100 passed. Handoff at sandbox-handoffs/teach-8xw.10.md.

title: Checker: verify domain facts in lesson text against source
description:
Checker stage, per the epic (bd show teach-8xw): "verify the domain facts
against source." Nothing exists yet. This needs to be a general mechanism
(different domains have different notions of "source" -- a math proof step
checked against the actual definition/theorem, a historical claim checked
against a citation, etc.) with per-domain source adapters, matching the
domain-plugin boundary from teach-8xw.4.

The biblical-text case has its own much more specific sourcing requirement
(BHS/Leningrad Codex + DSS + ancient versions for OT, NA27/28 + UBS4/5 for
NT) and is filed separately as teach-8xw.12 since it needs its own text-
source-access research before implementation.

What would close this: for at least the math domain (this repo's stated
test case is Dummit & Foote abstract algebra), a fact-checking pass that
takes an asserted claim from lesson text and a reference source and returns
confirmed / contradicted / cannot-verify -- with a runnable check using a
hand-written true claim, a hand-written false claim, and an ambiguous claim
that should abstain.
close_reason: Built teach/fact_checker.py (domain-agnostic claim-in/verdict-out engine, CONFIRMED/CONTRADICTED/CANNOT_VERIFY) + teach/math_facts.py (math domain adapter, 2 Dummit & Foote facts verified against actual theorem numbers) + tests/test_fact_checker.py (13 tests). Bead's 3 required hand-written examples (true/false/ambiguous) verify correctly via both python -m self-checks and pytest. uv run pytest -q: 69 passed. Handoff at sandbox-handoffs/teach-8xw.11.md.

title: Build the VA Math SOL prerequisite knowledge graph (mathgraph-style DAG)
description:
Producer stage: encode the Virginia Mathematics Standards of Learning as a
prerequisite DAG (nodes = concepts/standards, edges = "requires") -- the
mathgraph idea referenced by the epic (bd show teach-8xw). Repo currently has
no graph, no loader, no data at all (confirmed: `find /workspace -type f`
outside of tooling/config shows only pyproject.toml, sandbox files, README,
and a placeholder test -- no src/ or data/ directory exists).

Depends on teach-8xw.2 (survey for an existing, reusable graph -- do not
build this if a usable one already exists) and teach-8xw.4 (domain-plugin
schema decision, so this doesn't get built math-only and then need
reshaping).

What would close this: a loadable graph artifact (whatever format
teach-8xw.4 settles on) actually covering VA Math SOL strands, plus a
runnable check (per sandbox-prompt.md's "leave one runnable check behind")
that verifies the graph is a true DAG (no cycles) and that every edge
references a node that exists.
notes: Closed: built teach/va_math_sol_graph.py + teach/data/va_math_sol_k8.json (45 nodes = K-8 x 5 core strands, 40 precedes-edges chaining grades within each strand). Real VDOE-attributed standard text sourced live from learning-commons-org/knowledge-graph CDN (re-derived this session, not trusted secondhand from teach-8xw.2's handoff). Edge rule (grade N precedes N+1 within a strand) is disclosed as an inference, not claimed as VDOE-sourced -- self-check + a pytest test verify it against actual content escalation (K.NS counts to 100 -> 8.NS reaches the real number system), not just grade labels. HS course sequence out of scope, filed as teach-8xw.16. uv run pytest -q: 79 passed. Handoff: sandbox-handoffs/teach-8xw.5.md
close_reason: Loadable VA Math SOL K-8 prerequisite DAG built and tested per acceptance criteria: real sourced nodes, disclosed edge-derivation rule, runnable DAG/dangling-edge check (module self-check + 10 pytest tests), full suite passing (79 passed). HS extension filed separately as teach-8xw.16.

title: Producer: persona/narrative rendering of a graph traversal
description:
Producer stage: render a planned traversal of the prerequisite graph as
narrative through a "fluid persona," reusing narrator's story-generation
machinery (motive graph, personality as data structure) per the epic (bd
show teach-8xw). Nothing exists yet for this in the repo.

Hard-blocked on teach-8xw.1: there is currently no accessible `narrator`
package to reuse (see that bead for the negative-result search). Do not
start this by reimplementing a guessed version of narrator's API -- resolve
teach-8xw.1 first or the integration will need to be redone.

Also depends on teach-8xw.5 (needs a real graph to render traversals of) and
teach-8xw.4 (domain-plugin boundary, since this must work for non-math
domains too, not just the VA Math SOL case).

What would close this: given a traversal (sequence of graph nodes) and a
persona config, produces lesson narrative text, with a runnable check that
feeds it a small fixed traversal and asserts the output actually mentions
each node's concept (a cheap proxy for "the plan was followed," not a
substitute for the checker).
notes: Built teach/persona.py + tests/test_persona.py. Vendored Persona (Ocean, trimmed -- no CultureMatrix) and Backend protocol from narrator per teach-8xw.1's reusable-as-is split; render_traversal() renders a traversal via a persona through a pluggable Backend, defaulting to an offline deterministic TemplateBackend (mirrors motive.py's describe()/prose() split -- no live model in the self-check, same as every other producer/checker module in this repo). Self-check + 21 pytest tests verify: narrative mentions every node's concept in traversal order, boundary stays clean (check_no_forbidden_fields == []), empty/unknown traversal fails loud, Persona validates/round-trips, custom backends are swappable. uv run pytest -q: 121 passed. Handoff at sandbox-handoffs/teach-8xw.6.md.
close_reason: Acceptance criteria met: render_traversal(graph, traversal, persona, backend) renders a fixed traversal as persona-voiced narrative text; runnable check (module self-check + tests/test_persona.py) asserts output mentions each node's concept in order. Full test suite passes (121).

title: Producer: CBT primitives as pedagogical building blocks
description:
Producer stage: the epic (bd show teach-8xw) specifies cognitive behavioural
therapy primitives as the pedagogical building blocks -- e.g. structuring a
lesson around identifying a stuck belief ("I'm bad at math"), graded
exposure to harder problems, behavioral activation (small achievable next
step), spaced retrieval practice. None of this exists in the repo yet.

This is somewhat independent of the graph/persona machinery -- it can be
scoped as a small library of pedagogical "moves" (functions or data
templates) that the persona-rendering stage (teach-8xw.6) calls into when
turning a traversal into a lesson, but it needs its own definition of what
CBT primitive maps to what pedagogical moment before that integration can
happen.

What would close this: a named, enumerable set of CBT-derived pedagogical
primitives with a one-line definition of when each applies, plus a runnable
check that each primitive, given a minimal fake lesson context, produces
non-empty, on-topic output.
close_reason: Built teach/cbt_primitives.py: 4 named CBT primitives (identify_stuck_belief, graded_exposure, behavioral_activation, spaced_retrieval) matching the epic's own examples, each with a one-line when_to_use and a render function over a fake LessonMoment context. Runnable check (module self-check + 12 pytest tests, 46 total passing) proves each renders non-empty, on-topic output and raises on missing required context rather than guessing.

title: Find or stand up a common reference site for AI-consumable knowledge graphs
description:
The epic's PUBLISHING section has two distinct asks: (1) publish graphs this
repo builds to HuggingFace, and (2) separately, "find, or stand up, a common
reference site for existing knowledge graphs in an AI-consumable format" --
explicitly flagged in the epic text as "Survey first -- this may already
exist."

This is not yet surveyed. It is a different question from teach-8xw.2 (which
asks only whether a VA-SOL-specific graph already exists): this bead is about
whether there is a general registry/index of prerequisite-style knowledge
graphs (any domain) in a machine-consumable format, that this project should
either adopt as its publishing target or model its own HuggingFace dataset
schema on.

What would close this: a documented finding -- either a named existing
registry/site (with URL, format, and whether it accepts external
contributions) to target, or a documented negative result plus a decision
to stand up a minimal one (e.g. a HuggingFace dataset collection or a
GitHub-based index) alongside this project's own graph.
notes: Survey complete. Full write-up: sandbox-handoffs/teach-8xw.3.md. Found a real, active registry to target: 1EdTech CASE standard (native 'precedes' prerequisite-edge type), browsable/queryable now via open-source OpenSALT instance (opensalt.net, MIT licensed, active, real content incl. actual VA Math/English SOL uploaded by Virtual Virginia). Secondary general-purpose candidate: LOD Cloud (lod-cloud.net, 1683 datasets, open submission) for the literal 'any domain' reading, but not prerequisite-specific. Recommend modeling this project's own graph schema on CASE's CFItem/CFAssociation shape (teach-8xw.14/teach-8xw.5 decision, not done here) rather than standing up a new site.
close_reason: Positive finding: named existing registry (1EdTech CASE / OpenSALT, casenetwork.imsglobal.org) with URL, format (CASE JSON REST API, native 'precedes' prerequisite association type), and confirmed external-contribution capability (MIT-licensed self-hostable OpenSALT, real orgs incl. VDOE/Virtual Virginia already publishing into it). Documented in sandbox-handoffs/teach-8xw.3.md along with a secondary general-domain candidate (LOD Cloud). Closes without standing up a new site.

title: Decide the domain-plugin architecture before writing math-specific graph code
description:
The epic requires one engine to drive reading, writing, foreign language, and
arithmetic-through-undergraduate-mathematics, with "modularity is the point --
the same engine drives a live tutoring turn and a static curriculum
artifact." Nothing has been built yet (repo is scaffold-only: pyproject.toml
has zero dependencies, tests/ contains only a placeholder test, see
README.md "Status: scaffolded, nothing built").

Risk being filed pre-emptively but concretely: if the first real code is the
VA Math SOL graph loader/traversal engine (the most fleshed-out domain in the
epic), it is easy to accidentally bake math-specific assumptions (e.g. one
node = one SOL standard code, edge = strict prerequisite) into what should be
a domain-agnostic core (node = concept in some domain's standards, edge =
prerequisite relation, with domain-specific fact/answer-key formats attached
as data, not code).

What would close this: a short design decision (recorded via
`bd update <id> --design=...` on this bead, not a new doc file) fixing the
node/edge schema and the domain-plugin boundary -- what is shared engine code
vs. what is per-domain data/config -- before the graph-build bead
(teach-8xw.5, blocked on this) writes anything.
design:
DECISION (code: teach/concept_graph.py, tests: tests/test_concept_graph.py)

Node/edge schema, domain-agnostic:
- ConceptNode(id, domain, label, standard_ref=None, facts={}). `id` is an
  opaque globally-unique string each domain namespaces itself (e.g.
  "dummit-foote:3.1-normal-subgroups", "va-reading-sol:3.4-main-idea"); the
  engine never parses it. `domain` is a tag carried through, never branched
  on. `standard_ref` and `facts` are opaque per-domain payload (a SOL code /
  textbook section id, and whatever fact/answer-key shape that domain's
  producer+checker agree on) -- the engine stores and forwards them unread.
- PrerequisiteEdge(src, dst, type="precedes"). src must be established
  before dst -- same direction as CASE's `precedes` association ("origin
  before destination"), confirmed live against opensalt.net's CASE API in
  teach-8xw.3. This is the OPPOSITE direction from mathgraph's own
  `depends_on` edges (there, a claim depends_on the lemmas it uses, i.e.
  src needs dst first) -- teach-8xw.5 must invert direction if it ingests
  depends_on-shaped source data, not copy it uninspected. `type` is an open
  string, not an enum, so non-math domains needing another CASE relation
  (e.g. isPartOf) aren't forced to misuse "precedes".

Domain-plugin boundary -- shared engine vs. per-domain data/config:
- SHARED ENGINE (domain-ignorant, lives in teach/): ConceptNode/
  PrerequisiteEdge/ConceptGraph types; graph validation (duplicate ids,
  dangling edges, cycles -- raises GraphError rather than silently ordering
  an inconsistent graph); topological traversal. Already domain-agnostic
  elsewhere in the repo too: boundary.LessonArtifact and cbt_primitives'
  LessonMoment both operate on plain strings (concept_name), not a typed
  math object -- teach-8xw.7/.9 got this right before this bead existed.
- PER-DOMAIN DATA (not code; owned by e.g. teach-8xw.5 for VA Math SOL): the
  actual node/edge instances built from that domain's standards source, and
  the shape of `facts` for that domain.
- PER-DOMAIN CODE BEHIND A NARROW INTERFACE (reserved, not built by this
  bead): verifying a domain fact claim is genuine logic, not data, and must
  sit behind a claim-in/verdict-out function signature so the graph/
  traversal core never imports anything domain-specific. Designing that
  interface is teach-8xw.11's job; this bead only reserves the seam by
  keeping ConceptNode.facts opaque.

Verified: `uv run python3 -m teach.concept_graph` (one ConceptGraph carries
a math node and a reading node through the same traversal call with no
special-casing; a 2-node cycle is rejected, not silently ordered) and
`uv run pytest -q` -- 55 passed (46 pre-existing + 9 new in
tests/test_concept_graph.py covering: cross-domain traversal, opaque facts/
standard_ref, by_id lookup, duplicate-id rejection, dangling-edge rejection,
cycle rejection, open edge-type string, diamond-shaped (non-chain) DAG).
close_reason: Design decision recorded via --design; teach/concept_graph.py + tests/test_concept_graph.py embody it; teach-8xw.5/.6/.11 now unblocked

title: Tutor that plans on a knowledge graph, checked by a solver blind to the plan
description:
One engine, two front-ends: interactive 1:1 tutoring and static curriculum
development. See sandbox-prompt.md for the claim and why it is hard.

PRODUCER (plans and delivers)
- Prerequisite knowledge graph, mathgraph-style DAG. Seed: Virginia
  Mathematics Standards of Learning. Look for an existing graph that already
  covers the VA SOL before building one.
- Fluid persona that renders a graph traversal as narrative, reusing
  narrator's story-generation machinery (motive graph, personality as data
  structure) rather than reimplementing it.
- CBT primitives as the pedagogical building blocks.
- Cialdini (Influence, Pre-Suasion) to guide the learner toward excellence,
  bounded by the honesty constraint below.
- Multi-disciplinary: reading, writing, foreign language, arithmetic through
  undergraduate mathematics. Modularity is the point -- the same engine drives
  a live tutoring turn and a static curriculum artifact.

CHECKER (must not see producer internals)
Sees only what the learner saw: emitted lesson text. No planner target node,
no traversal, no answer key. From that alone:
- recover which concept was taught and which prerequisites it assumed
- verify domain facts against source
- flag any promise about learner potential that outruns what effort delivers

HONESTY CONSTRAINT
Encourage honestly with what hard work can actually achieve. Never inflate
potential. This is a checkable property, not a tone note.

TEXTUAL FIDELITY
Where instruction touches biblical text, judge against sources, never model
recollection: OT = BHS / Leningrad Codex, with Dead Sea Scrolls and ancient
versions (Septuagint, Samaritan Pentateuch, Syriac Peshitta) for variants;
NT = Nestle-Aland 27/28 and UBS 4/5.

PUBLISHING
Publish graphs we build to HuggingFace (HF_TOKEN is forwarded). Separately:
find, or stand up, a common reference site for existing knowledge graphs in
an AI-consumable format. Survey first -- this may already exist.

TEST CASE
Teach Dummit & Foote to a learner whose stated interest is James Bond. The
checker must confirm the algebra is correct and the prerequisites were really
established -- not that the Bond framing was enjoyable.

title: Verify publish_graph.py live push against a real HF dataset repo
description: teach-8xw.14 built teach/publish_graph.py with a dry-run path (fully tested, no network) and a live-push path (dry_run=False, calls huggingface_hub.HfApi.create_repo/upload_file) that this sandbox could not test -- HF_TOKEN was unset in the teach-8xw.14 session. The dry-run tests only prove the exported files are shaped correctly, not that a real push to huggingface.co with a real token actually succeeds (auth works, repo_type='dataset' is accepted, files land with correct content, exist_ok=True doesn't clobber unexpectedly on a second push). Needs a session with a live HF_TOKEN and a disposable/test HF namespace to publish into.
acceptance_criteria: A session with a real HF_TOKEN runs 'python3 -m teach.publish_graph --repo-id <disposable-repo> --live' (or calls publish(..., dry_run=False) directly), confirms the repo was created on huggingface.co, confirms nodes.jsonl/associations.jsonl/manifest.json/README.md are present with correct content, and records the repo_id used and result in a handoff so a future session can inspect or clean it up.
notes: Filed from teach-8xw.14. Not a blocker for that bead's acceptance criteria (dry-run mode + a runnable check covering it), which is fully met without this.

title: Extend VA Math SOL graph to high school course sequence (Algebra I/Geometry/Algebra II/...)
description: teach-8xw.5 built the VA Math SOL prerequisite DAG for grades K-8 only (teach/va_math_sol_graph.py, teach/data/va_math_sol_k8.json): 45 grade-strand groupings, edges chained by grade number within each of the 5 core strands (NS/CE/MG/PFA/PS). Virginia's high-school math standards (grades 9-12) are organized by *course* (Algebra I 'A', Geometry 'G', Algebra II 'A2', AFDA, plus electives Computer Math 'CM' and Discrete Math 'DM') rather than a single linear grade number, so the K-8 grade-chain rule doesn't apply -- course sequencing (e.g. Algebra I precedes Geometry precedes Algebra II) needs its own sourced justification. This session could not reach a VDOE-published course-sequence document to source that ordering (doe.virginia.gov returns 403 to bot traffic -- Akamai block, confirmed live; Wayback CDX has zero archived snapshots of any VDOE crosswalk/sequence page -- see teach-8xw.2's and teach-8xw.5's handoffs for the exact checks run). The Learning Commons dataset (github.com/learning-commons-org/knowledge-graph, CC BY-4.0) does have the real HS course-strand 'Standard Grouping' nodes (statementCodes like A.EI, G.PC, A2.F, etc, all tagged gradeLevel 9-12 with no finer grade signal) -- same source teach-8xw.5 used for K-8 -- so the node text is available; only the course-ordering edges are missing.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) a sourced VA-specific course-sequence document is found (VDOE, Wayback, or another citable source) and used to add course-level PrerequisiteEdges to the graph with the source cited in code, or (b) the negative result is documented (no sourced VA-specific course sequence reachable) and the bead closes with that finding rather than inventing an unsourced ordering. Either way: a runnable check (DAG validity, no dangling edges) covering whatever is added, same as teach-8xw.5's.

title: Checker: research biblical-text source access (BHS/Leningrad Codex, DSS, NA27/28, UBS4/5)
description:
The epic (bd show teach-8xw) and sandbox-prompt.md both specify that any
instruction touching biblical text must be checked against specific critical
editions, never model recollection: BHS/Leningrad Codex with Dead Sea
Scrolls and ancient-version variants (Septuagint, Samaritan Pentateuch,
Syriac Peshitta) for the Old Testament, and Nestle-Aland 27/28 with UBS 4/5
for the New. None of this has been surveyed yet -- I have not confirmed
whether any of these critical texts are available in a machine-readable,
programmatically queryable form under a license that permits this project
to use them, which is a prerequisite to implementing the fidelity checker
at all.

This is filed as a research task, separate from teach-8xw.11 (general
domain-fact verification) and separate from actually implementing the
checker module, because the licensing/access question could materially
change what's implementable (e.g. NA28 is copyrighted and not freely
redistributable in full; BHS/Leningrad Codex has more open digital
editions like the Westminster Leningrad Codex; UBS text is also
copyrighted). Get this wrong and the checker module gets built against a
source it can't legally or technically use in production.

What would close this: for each of the four source requirements (BHS/
Leningrad Codex, DSS variants, NA27/28, UBS4/5), a documented answer to
"is there a digital, queryable edition available, under what license, and
what if anything is a legally usable substitute (e.g. SBLGNT as an open
alternative apparatus-compatible-enough proxy for NA)."
